what: Airbnb runs a marketplace for short-term stays. More than five million hosts list homes and rooms, guests book through the site, and Airbnb takes a fee from both sides. It has added experiences and local services on top of stays.
customers: Travellers in over 220 countries and the individual hosts and small property managers who list with it.
money: service fees charged to guests and hosts on each night booked
activities, and services such as chefs and photographers offered to guests
moat: Supply that hotels cannot match, built one home at a time over nearly two decades, and a brand so strong that people use it as a verb.
risks: Cities keep restricting or banning short-term rentals
Growth in nights booked has slowed into the low teens
Hotel groups and Booking.com now list private homes too
Any safety or trust failure damages the brand quickly
opportunities: Gross margins above 80% and strong free cash flow fund large buybacks
New experiences and services can lift revenue per trip without adding homes
Expansion outside the US and Europe is still early in many markets
watch: Nights and experiences booked, and whether the new services generate real revenue.
